Rashi on Niddah 12a:10:1.hebrew: לטהרות בעיא בדיקה - כלומר, העסוקה בטהרות בעיא בדיקה אפילו לבעלה:
Rashi on Niddah 12a:10:1.english: For ritually pure items, she requires an examination - That is to say, [a woman] who is engaged in [handling] ritually pure items requires an examination even for [relations with] her husband.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:10:2.english: For her husband, she does not require an examination - Where she is not engaged [with pure items].

Rashi on Niddah 12a:10:3.hebrew: אין לה וסת אפילו לבעלה - גרידא, דאינה עסוקה בטהרות, בעיא בדיקה:
Rashi on Niddah 12a:10:3.english: [If] she does not have a fixed cycle, even for her husband - [For her husband] alone, when she is not engaged in [ritually] pure items, she requires an examination.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:10:4.english: Any [case] for her husband - Without [involvement in] ritual purities.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:10:5.hebrew: לא בעיא בדיקה - אפילו אין לה וסת. הילכך, הא דאמר שמואל אסורה לשמש עד שתבדוק, בעסוקה [בטהרות] קאי, והיינו דאמר לעיל: ואוקימנא בעסוקה בטהרות:
Rashi on Niddah 12a:10:5.english: Does not require an examination - Even if she does not have a fixed cycle. Therefore, that which Shmuel said, "She is forbidden to engage in intercourse until she examines [herself]," refers to [a woman who is] handling [pure items]; and that is what [the Gemara] said earlier: "And we established [it] as referring to [a woman] handling pure items."

Rashi on Niddah 12a:13:1.english: Since he requested of her - For marital relations.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:13:2.hebrew: אין לך בדיקה גדולה מזו - דאי לא קים לה דטהורה היא, הוה בדקה. ובדיקה דקאמר שמואל לעיל, בתביעה סגי? ולבי מגמגם:
Rashi on Niddah 12a:13:2.english: There is no greater examination than this - For if it were not clear to her that she is pure, she would have examined [herself]. And [as for] the examination that Shmuel stated above, does a request suffice? And my heart hesitates.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:13:3.english: In accordance with this baraita - [Does she] require examination or a request?

Rashi on Niddah 12a:2:1.hebrew: כשיעור וסת - מיד לאחר בעילה. בחטאת — דאמרינן לקמן בפ"ב (נדה דף יד.): נמצא על סדין שלה אותיום, כלומר מיד לאחר בעילה — חייבין בקרבן, דודאי דם הוה בשעת ביאה:
Rashi on Niddah 12a:2:1.english: Within the period of a veset - Immediately after intercourse. [And as for rendering him liable] for a sin offering—as we say later in chapter 2 (Niddah 14a): "[If blood] was found on her sheet otyom"—that is to say, immediately after intercourse—"they are liable to [bring] an offering," for there was certainly blood at the time of intercourse.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:3:1.hebrew: לבדיקה - לחורין ולסדקין, הילכך כשיעור וסת לא משכחת לה:
Rashi on Niddah 12a:3:1.english: For an examination - [Which is] into the crevices and folds; therefore, you cannot find it [performed] within the time span of a *veset*.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:3:2.english: To the male organ - The [male] organ.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:3:3.english: And an examination cloth - A cloth with which she wipes herself.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:4:1.hebrew: לקינוח - מבחוץ. אם בקינוח מצאה דם בכשיעור הזה, חייבין חטאת. אבל אם בבדיקתה מצאה, כבר ארך השיעור, שהרי לא בצד המשקוף עומד, אלא בידה אוחזתו, ויש כאן שיעור עודף כדי הבאה מידה למשקוף, ואשם תלוי איכא, ולא חטאת:
Rashi on Niddah 12a:4:1.english: For wiping - [Wiping] externally. If she found blood through wiping within this timeframe, they are liable for a sin offering. But if she found [blood] through her [internal] examination, the timeframe has already lengthened, for [the cloth] does not stand alongside the doorpost [the entrance]; rather, she holds it in her hand, and there is an excess amount of time here [equal to] the time it takes to bring [it] from her hand to the doorpost, and there is [liability for] a provisional guilt offering, but not a sin offering.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:4:2.hebrew: מהו שתקנח - אשה שאינה עסוקה בטהרות, מי בעיא קינוח לאחר תשמיש כשיעור וסת, לידע אם תמצא דם ויהא בעלה חייב חטאת:
Rashi on Niddah 12a:4:2.english: What is [the ruling as to whether] she should wipe - Does a woman who is not engaged in [handling] ritually pure items require wiping after intercourse within the duration of an interval, to know whether she will find blood and her husband will be liable for a sin-offering?

Rashi on Niddah 12a:5:1.english: What is [the halakha as to whether] she should examine - An actual examination.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:5:2.hebrew: באשם תלוי - דאמרינן לקמן (שם:), נמצא על שלה לאחר זמן, יותר מכשיעור וסת, חייבין באשם תלוי, דספק הוה דם בשעת ביאה, ספק בא לאחר מכאן:
Rashi on Niddah 12a:5:2.english: For a provisional guilt offering - For we say later (ibid., 14b): If [blood] was found on hers after time, more than the duration of an interval, they are liable for a provisional guilt offering, as it is uncertain whether there was blood at the time of intercourse or whether it came after that.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:5:3.english: If so - That you require her to examine [herself] after intercourse.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:5:4.hebrew: לבו נוקפו - קודם ביאה. והא דתנן לקמן (שם.) דרך בנות ישראל משמשות בשני עדים — בעסוקות בטהרות:
Rashi on Niddah 12a:5:4.english: His heart strikes him - Prior to intercourse. And that which we learned later in the mishna (ibid.): "The practice of Jewish women is to engage in marital relations with two examination cloths" — [that is] with regard to women engaged in [handling] ritually pure items.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:6:1.hebrew: וזהו עדן של צנועות - כלומר, מדת חסידות שנו כאן, ולאו חיובא הוא, דאמרינן בפרק שני (שם.): הצנועות מתקנות להן שלישי לתקן את הבית. זהו עדן — אלפני תשמיש קאי:
Rashi on Niddah 12a:6:1.english: And this is the examination cloth of virtuous women - That is to say, they taught a standard of piety here, and it is not an obligation, for we say in the second chapter (ibid.): "The virtuous women prepare a third [cloth] for themselves to prepare the house." "This is their examination cloth" refers to [the one used] before intercourse.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:7:1.hebrew: אין בודקת בו לפני תשמיש אחר - לפי שמטונף וכהה מראית ליבונו בבדיקה ראשונה, ושוב אין נראית בו טיפה כחרדל:
Rashi on Niddah 12a:7:1.english: She does not examine with it before another act of intercourse - Because it is soiled and the appearance of its whiteness was dimmed in the first examination, and a drop [the size of] a mustard seed will no longer be visible on it.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:8:1.hebrew: יש לה וסת לא בעיא בדיקה - בתמיה: והא קתני מתניתין ביש לה וסת דבעיא בדיקה, כיון דעסוקה בטהרות? ולקמן פריך: לישני ליה הא בשאינה עסוקה בטהרות, ומשני: קסבר שמואל כי אינה עסוקה, אפילו אין לה וסת לא בעיא בדיקה לבעלה, הואיל ואינה עסוקה בטהרות:
Rashi on Niddah 12a:8:1.english: [If] she has a fixed cycle, she does not require an examination - [This was asked] in astonishment: For doesn't the mishna teach regarding [a woman who] has a fixed cycle that she requires an examination, since she is engaged in [handling] ritually pure items? And later [the Gemara] asks: Let him answer him that this is when she is not engaged in [handling] ritually pure items! And [the Gemara] answers: Shmuel holds that when she is not engaged [in handling them], even [if] she does not have a fixed cycle, she does not require an examination for [intercourse with] her husband, since she is not engaged in [handling] ritually pure items.

Rashi on Niddah 12a:9:1.hebrew: ערה - דחזיא לעסוקי בטהרות, בעיא בדיקה לבעלה. אי נמי: דליכא טירחא לצעורה, אבל ישנה – איכא צערא, ולא אטרחוה רבנן. אי נמי: ישנה, דלא חזיא לטהרות – אפילו רגילה לעסוק בטהרות לא בעיא בדיקה:
Rashi on Niddah 12a:9:1.english: Awake - Since she is fit to engage in [handling] ritually pure items [taharot], she requires an examination [even] for [intercourse with] her husband. Alternatively, [it is] because there is no burden to cause her distress [when awake]; but [when she is] asleep, there is distress, and the Sages did not burden her. Alternatively: [as for] a sleeping woman, since she is not fit to engage in ritually pure items [while asleep], even if she is accustomed to engage in ritually pure items, she does not require an examination.

Tosafot on Niddah 12a:11:1.hebrew: בין ישנות - פי' דליכא איסור נדות, אבל אסור לבא על הישנה, כדאמר בנדרים (כ:). א"נ, הכא לא לגמרי בישנה איירי, אלא אינה ערה כל כך שתדע להשיב אם היא טהורה אם לאו:
Tosafot on Niddah 12a:11:1.english: Whether [they are] sleeping - The explanation is that there is no prohibition of *niddah*, but it is forbidden to have relations with a sleeping woman, as [the Gemara] says in Nedarim (20b). Alternatively, here it is not dealing with [a woman who is] completely asleep, but rather she is not awake enough to know to reply whether she is pure or not.

Tosafot on Niddah 12a:12:1.hebrew: שמואל במאי מוקי לה - וא"ת: ולוקמה באינה עסוקה בטהרות? ויש לומר, דדייק מלישנא יתירא, דקתני: נשיהם להם בחזקת טהרה, ואמאי איצטריך תו למיתני: ובאין ושוהים עמהם? אלא לגלויי דאיירי דעסוקה בטהרות. ובפ"ב (לקמן נדה דף טו.), דקתני: כל הנשים בחזקת טהרה, וקתני בתר הכי: והבאין מן הדרך נשיהם להם בחזקת טהרה, וקתני תרתי אע"ג דאינה עסוקה בטהרות איירי — התם אשמועינן דאין לחלק בין באין מן הדרך לבני העיר. וא"ת: בלא שמואל תקשי מתניתין, דמצרכת בדיקה בעסוקה בטהרות, אברייתא דהכא? וי"ל, דפריך לשמואל אפילו בישנה באין לה וסת, אבל מתני' לא מיירי בישנה; וכן פי' רשב"ם. [א"נ, ממתני' ה"מ לדחוקי ולאוקומי באין לה וסת, ודיה שעתה לא קאי אלא אצריכה להיות בודקת ותו לא, אע"ג דפשטא דמתניתין ביש לה וסת, כדפריך לעיל: והא מתניתין ביש לה וסת עסקינן]:
Tosafot on Niddah 12a:12:1.english: With regard to what does Shmuel establish it - And if you say: Let him establish it [as referring to a woman who] is not engaged in [handling] ritually pure items (*taharot*)? Then one can say that he infers [this] from the superfluous phrasing, as it teaches: "their wives are to them in a presumptive status of purity" — and why was it further necessary to teach: "and they come and stay with them"? Rather, [it comes] to reveal that it is dealing with [a woman who] is engaged in [handling] ritually pure items. And [as for that which is taught] in the second chapter (below, Niddah 15a), where it teaches: "All women are in a presumptive status of purity," and it teaches after this: "and those returning from a journey, their wives are to them in a presumptive status of purity" — and it teaches both, even though it is dealing with [a case where] she is not engaged in [handling] ritually pure items — there, it informs us that one should not differentiate between those returning from a journey and city residents. And if you say: Even without Shmuel, let our mishna — which requires an examination in [the case of a woman] engaged in [handling] ritually pure items — pose a difficulty against the baraita here? And one can say that it raises a difficulty against Shmuel even in [the case of a woman who is] sleeping [and] has no fixed cycle, whereas our mishna does not deal with [a woman who is] sleeping; and so explained Rashbam. [Alternatively, from our mishna one could have forced [an interpretation] and established it [as referring to a woman] who does not have a fixed cycle, and [explained that the phrase] "her time is sufficient" refers only to "she is required to examine herself" and nothing more, even though the simple reading of our mishna is [that it deals with a woman] who has a fixed cycle, as [the Gemara] asked above: "And does not our mishna deal with [a woman] who has a fixed cycle?"]

Tosafot on Niddah 12a:13:1.hebrew: כיון שתבעה - פירוש: כיון שבא מן הדרך, מפייסה ותובעה לתשמיש, ואי חזיא, כבר רמיא אנפשה שהרגישה בשעת ראייה וזוכרת; אבל אם לא בא מן הדרך, אסור בערה, לפי שאינו מאריך בפיוס של תשמיש, אלא בא עליה מיד, ולא רמיא אנפשה לאזכורי שהרגישה:
Tosafot on Niddah 12a:13:1.english: Since he requested of her - Explanation: Since he has returned from a journey, he appeases her and solicits her for intercourse; and if she had seen [blood], she would already have put her mind [to it], as she experienced a sensation (hargashah) at the time of seeing, and she would remember [it]. But if he did not return from a journey, [relations with her while she is] awake is forbidden [without an examination], because he does not prolong the appeasement for intercourse, but rather engages with her immediately, and she does not put her mind to recalling whether she experienced a sensation.

Tosafot on Niddah 12a:13:2.hebrew: מהו למעבד כי הא מתניתא - פי' רש"י: כי הא מתניתא — דבעיא בדיקה או תביעה. וקשה, דבערה דוקא מצריך בדיקה; ואם כן, מאי קא מהדר ליה דמגניא באפיה? דבתביעה לא מגניא באפיה! ועוד, אי לבעלה גרידא קבעי — כדמשמע, דלבני בבל היה שואל — הא פשיטא, דאמר לעיל (נדה דף יא:): כל לבעלה לא בעיא בדיקה, וגם אין להחמיר לבדוק, דא"כ לבו נוקפו ופורש, כדאמר לעיל. ואי בעסוקה בטהרות קבעי, פשיטא שצריכה בדיקה, כדתנן: ובשעה שהיא עוברת לשמש ביתה כו'! ותו, למה תולה בעייתו בברייתא זו, כיון דמתניתין נמי מצרכה בדיקה לטהרות? ונראה לפרש: מהו למעבד כי הא מתניתא — דלא מצרכה מידי בישנה; דשמא אף לבעלה גרידא צריך להקיצה ולתובעה? והא דאמרינן לעיל דאפילו באין לה וסת לא בעיא בדיקה לבעלה, בישנה מ"מ דילמא תביעה בעיא. אי נמי, לעיל איירי כשהוא בעיר, דאם איתא דהיתה טמאה — הוה אמרה ליה קודם לכן; אבל בבא מן הדרך, איכא למיחש. ומתני' דפ"ב (לקמן נדה טו.) דבאין מן הדרך נשיהם להם בחזקת טהרה, איכא נמי למימר: דהיינו דלא בעו בדיקה, אבל בעו תביעה; אי נמי, בערות דווקא; אי נמי, ביש לה וסת:
Tosafot on Niddah 12a:13:2.english: What is [the halakha with regard to] acting in accordance with this baraita? - Rashi explained: "In accordance with this baraita" — that she requires an examination or a request. And this is difficult, for it is specifically when she is awake that [the Gemara] requires an examination; and if so, why does [Rava] respond to him: "[No,] lest she be demeaned before him"? For with a request, she is not demeaned before him! And furthermore, if he was asking [only regarding intercourse] with her husband alone — as is implied, since he was asking for the people of Babylonia — this is obvious, for [the Gemara] said above (Niddah 11b): Anything [done only] for her husband does not require an examination, and one should also not be stringent to examine, for if so, his heart will smite him and he will withdraw, as [the Gemara] said above. And if he was asking regarding [a woman who is] engaged in [handling] pure items (taharot), it is obvious that she requires an examination, as we learned in the Mishnah: "And at the time she passes to serve her house, etc."! And furthermore, why does he hang his question on this baraita, given that our Mishnah also requires an examination for taharot? And it seems [correct] to explain: "What is [the halakha with regard to] acting in accordance with this baraita" — which does not require anything when she is asleep; for perhaps even [for intercourse] with her husband alone, one must awaken her and request of her? And as for that which we said above, that even [for a woman] who has no fixed cycle she does not require an examination for her husband, nevertheless, when she is asleep, perhaps she requires a request. Alternatively, above is dealing with [a case] where he was in town, so that if it were so that she had become impure, she would have told him beforehand; but when he comes from a journey, there is [reason] to be concerned. And [as for] the Mishnah of the second chapter (below, Niddah 15a), that [with regard to] those who come from a journey, their wives are in a presumptive status of ritual purity for them — one can also say that this means that they do not require an examination, but they do require a request; alternatively, [that Mishnah refers] specifically to when they are awake; alternatively, when she has a fixed cycle.

Tosafot on Niddah 12a:1:1.english: Rabbi Zeira raised a dilemma: What is [the halakha as to whether] a woman should examine [herself] - Meaning, before intercourse.

Tosafot on Niddah 12a:1:2.hebrew: לבו נוקפו ופורש - פר"ח: כיון דרואה אשתו בודקת, מחשב שאם לא הרגישה לא היתה בודקת, לפי שיודעת שחכמים לא תקנו לבדוק:
Tosafot on Niddah 12a:1:2.english: His heart strikes him and he separates - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: Since he sees his wife examining [herself], he reasons that if she had not felt [a sensation], she would not have examined [herself], because she knows that the Sages did not institute [a requirement] to examine.

Tosafot on Niddah 12a:2:1.hebrew: כדי לחייב בעלה חטאת - הכא נמי הוה מצי למיבעי: מהו שתבדוק קודם תשמיש ותניח העד עד הבקר כדי לחייב בעלה חטאת? אלא דכבר השיב לו, שאם תבדוק לפני תשמיש, לבו נוקפו ופורש:
Tosafot on Niddah 12a:2:1.english: In order to render her husband liable to a sin-offering - Here, too, he could have asked: What is [the halakha as to whether] she may examine [herself] before intercourse and leave the examination cloth until morning in order to render her husband liable to a sin-offering? Rather, [he did not ask this] because he had already answered him that if she examines [herself] before intercourse, his heart strikes him [with apprehension] and he separates [from her].

Tosafot on Niddah 12a:7:1.hebrew: צנוע לא מיקרי רשע לא מיקרי - בתמיה. וא"ת: בריש כתובות (דף ב:) דאמר משום צנועות ומשום פרוצות, כיון דקרי להו צנועות, הנהו דלא עבדי הכי אמאי קרי להו פרוצות? וי"ל, דהתם קרי להו צנועות כדאמרינן התם, זמנין דלא אניס וסברה דאניס, ואע"ג שבדין היה לה לתלות שאין אניס, דרוב העולם אינן אנוסים. ופרוצות, משום דזימנין דאנוס; פירוש: פעמים דיודעת שהוא אנוס ואמרה דלא אנוס; ול"ג התם וסברה:
Tosafot on Niddah 12a:7:1.english: He is not called virtuous, [but] he is not called wicked - [This is stated] in astonishment. And if you say: At the beginning of Ketubot (2b), where [Rava] says [that an unavoidable accident does not cancel a bill of divorce] "because of virtuous women and because of licentious women" — since he calls them "virtuous women", why does he call those who do not act this way "licentious women"? And one can say that there, he calls them "virtuous women" as we say there: "Sometimes he was not unavoidably detained, and she thinks that he was unavoidably detained" — even though by law she was entitled to assume that he was not unavoidably detained, as the majority of the world are not unavoidably detained. And [they are called] "licentious women" because "sometimes he was unavoidably detained" — the explanation is: sometimes she knows that he was unavoidably detained, yet she says that he was not unavoidably detained; and we do not read there [in the text]: "and she thinks" (ve-savra).

Tosafot on Niddah 12a:8:1.hebrew: אשה שאין לה וסת אסורה לשמש עד שתבדוק - ובעסוקה בטהרות איירי. וא"ת: מאי קמ"ל? מתניתין היא (לעיל נדה יא.): ובשעה שהיא עוברת לשמש את ביתה! וליכא למימר דאתא לאשמועינן, דאע"ג דאין לה וסת דמותר לקיימה על ידי בדיקה כר"ח בן אנטיגנוס, וכן פירש רש"י לקמן; דהלשון משמע דלא בא להשמיענו היתרא, אלא להשמיענו שצריכה בדיקה. וי"ל, דקמ"ל באין לה וסת, דאפילו ישנה צריכה בדיקה:
Tosafot on Niddah 12a:8:1.english: A woman who does not have a fixed cycle is forbidden to engage in intercourse until she examines [herself] - And it is dealing with [a woman] who is engaged in [handling] ritually pure items (tahorot). And if you say: What is this coming to teach us? It is [already taught in] our mishna (above, Niddah 11a): "And at the time that she is about to engage in intercourse with her husband" [she must examine herself]! And one cannot say that it comes to teach us that even though she does not have a fixed cycle, it is permitted to maintain her [as a wife] by means of examination, in accordance with Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus — and so Rashi explained below — for the phrasing implies that it did not come to teach us a permission, but rather to teach us that she requires an examination. And it can be answered that it comes to teach us regarding [a woman] who does not have a fixed cycle, that even [when she is] asleep, she requires an examination.
